  Threat: Threat in Delays: When something takes longer than expected I assume something bad is happening, Startle to Sounds: I jump or startle at ordinary sounds that would not bother most people, Threat from Strangers: I feel threatened by strangers approaching me even in ordinary situations
  Memory: Terror on Recall: Remembering the event brings back the same terror I felt at the time, More Real Than Normal: My memories of the event feel more real and vivid than memories of ordinary things, Story Feels Unreal: The memory is so extreme it is hard to believe it actually happened to me

Vignette:
Kai Ahina's mind was still back in that police station cell, reliving the terror he felt the night his world turned upside down. It had been three years since the incident, but the memory remained more real and vivid than any ordinary recollection. He could smell the disinfectant, taste the dry air, and feel the cold metal bench beneath him. The story was so extreme it was hard to believe it actually happened to him – a law-abiding citizen, a respected airline pilot, a divorced father of two. That fateful night, Kai had been driving home from a late-night flight when he was pulled over by police for a minor traffic infraction. What should have been a routine stop escalated into a chaotic scene: loud voices, flashing lights, and Kai being dragged out of his car and thrown to the ground. He remembered feeling nauseous as he lay there, helpless, with officers standing over him, their faces twisted in anger. In the months that followed, Kai began to notice changes in himself. Physical proximity to strangers made him anxious – a crowded airport terminal or a packed flight cabin would send his heart racing. Driving with others was also becoming increasingly difficult; every time someone got into the car with him, he couldn't shake off the feeling of being trapped and vulnerable. Even simple tasks like grocery shopping became overwhelming as he found himself jumping at ordinary sounds: the rustling of bags, the beeping of cash registers. Kai's colleagues started to notice a change in him too. Delays on flights, which were once minor inconveniences, now sent him spiraling into worst-case scenarios. "Something bad is happening," his mind would whisper as he waited for clearance or navigated through air traffic control. His startle response became notorious among the cabin crew – they'd learn to warn him before opening the cockpit door or making any sudden announcements. As time went on, Kai's world shrunk further. He stopped attending social gatherings, fearing encounters with strangers would trigger another episode of crippling anxiety. His relationship with his children suffered as he found it harder to spend quality time with them; even playdates at the park became fraught with tension as he scanned the surroundings for potential threats. Kai's airline began to notice a decline in his performance too. Flights were delayed or cancelled due to "unforeseen circumstances," and Kai knew that deep down, it was his own fears holding him back. The thought of losing his job, his reputation, and his sense of purpose became unbearable. It was this fear that finally pushed Kai to seek help. As he sat in the therapist's office, Kai couldn't shake off the feeling of unease – a familiar sensation by now. He fidgeted with his hands, avoiding eye contact as he recounted his story. What frightened him most was losing control again, reliving that night in the police station cell. Yet, it was this same fear that brought him here, to confront the memories and emotions he'd been trying to outrun for so long. Kai's journey towards healing had just begun – a daunting task ahead, but one he knew he could no longer avoid.
